title: The completion of a discrete valuation ring is a discrete valuation ring
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local domain whose maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ is generated by a single nonzero element (a discrete valuation ring, Stacks Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (4)), and let $A^\wedge=\varprojlim_nA/\mathfrak m^n$ be its $\mathfrak m$-adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Then $A^\wedge$ is a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by a single nonzero element; that is, $A^\wedge$ is again a discrete valuation ring.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0AP1 (lemma-completion-dvr), direction 'A DVR implies A^ DVR'; its proof uses More on Algebra Lemmas lemma-completion-dimension and lemma-completion-regular and Algebra Lemma Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr)

proof.text: A DVR is a local principal ideal domain. Mathlib.RingTheory.RegularLocalRing.Defs supplies the instance IsRegularLocalRing A for a local principal ideal domain, realizing the regular-local definition [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Mathlib IsDiscreteValuationRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one gives dim A = 1. These are the implication (1) to (3) of Stacks 00PD.

Apply AdicCompletion.isRegularLocalRing_iff A [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local] in the forward direction to obtain regularity of the maximal-ideal completion B. Apply the first conjunct of RingTheory.completion_dimension A [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension], followed by the DVR dimension equality, to obtain dim B = dim A = 1.
The instance IsRegularLocalRing.isDomain B [lem-sc-regular-local-domain] makes the regular local ring B a domain. This supplies the explicit domain witness required by the existential conclusion.

Apply the already proved IsRegularLocalRing.isDiscreteValuationRing B [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr] to regularity and dim B = 1. Pair this DVR proof with the domain instance. This is the implication (3) to (1) of Stacks 00PD; it includes the nonzero principal maximal ideal argument, so no separate uniformizer or maximal-ideal calculation is needed here.
